data.content_ref: inline:Two-level warrant validity: split attack edges into provisional and committed based on an inner grounded labelling of a warrant graph. First compute grounded extension on the subgraph of warrants only; then construct the outer attack relation using only attacks whose warrant node is accepted; finally compute the grounded extension on that derived graph. This gives a compositional, polynomial two-pass semantics and preserves root validity because roots are untouched by warrant filtering. Weakness: the inner and outer labellings are not mutually recursive; an attack on a warrant by an argument that is only accepted in the outer labelling is invisible to the inner pass, so some self-referential challenges to warrants are missed.
